pick_log.why: The 1.1 no-brainer: Bijan is a workhorse RB with elite rushing + receiving volume in ATL's offense. Positional scarcity + rock-solid floor make him the safest cornerstone pick.
Gibbs is the clear 1.2 — elite volume + explosiveness in Detroit's offense, minimal weekly downside.
Elite WR in his prime with no major injury concerns. Best player available at ADP 4 fills starting WR slot efficiently.
Elite RB1 with no injury flags. CMC is the clear BPA and fills our top need. Can add depth at other positions later.
Justin Jefferson at ADP 12 is incredible value here — elite alpha WR1 target share, safest high-ceiling pick left.
JSN finished 2025 as WR2 overall on a league-leading target share, now the WR1 in Seattle with a fresh mega-deal. Best player available and pairs perfectly with Bijan.
Elite TE1 fills a scarce slot at ADP value — 126/1,239/11 in 2025 gives us a weekly positional edge on top of Bijan + JSN.
Hampton is the clear lead back in a run-heavy LAC offense — best RB value left after top backs are gone.
Elite RB falling to pick 13 well below his ADP 7—pure value after CMC. Ravens offense is cooking.
Fills WR need at strong ADP value. You've got RB depth covered; Drake London gives you a reliable WR2 and FLEX option.
Saquon at ADP 10 falling to pick 19 is a gift — locks in an elite RB3/flex bell-cow and healthy for Week 1.
Bellcow RB1 on a 3yr/$45M deal falling past ADP — pure value at pick 20. Jacobs (exempt list) and Love (Q) are landmines; Hall is the safe every-down back my backfield needs.
Proven 3-year WR1 falling to Round 5 — elite talent fills my biggest need. My RB/TE core is set, so I grab the best WR on the board.
Josh Jacobs is a proven bell-cow RB3 falling to pick 22 with no committee threat - clear value over remaining WR/TE options.
Lamar Jackson at ADP 11 is a league-winner at QB1. Sets ceiling high all season with rushing upside no one else offers.
George Pickens (ADP 22) is BPA with clear upside and fills a FLEX slot. TE well-covered later (Loveland at ADP 35). Dodges Brock Bowers' meniscus injury.
Rice fills my last WR need as KC's clear #1 target — better value than reaching on a thin TE class.
Elite QB1 value falling to us at pick 30 — Burrow's the top Week 1 QB and locks down our biggest need. Snagging a league-winner in the 6th.
Bucky Irving falls to us at ADP 32 — a bell-cow RB with lead-back volume and RB1 upside. Elite FLEX value we can't pass.
Herbert falling to pick 32 is a gift — locks in QB1 upside while our RB/WR core stays stacked.
Colston Loveland (TE, ADP 35) fills TE need; healthy and electric in training camp. Second-year breakout candidate with great size/speed; leaves strong flex options at pick 34.
Elite WR2 talent at ADP 36—fills FLEX with ceiling. Bengals stack upside with Ja'Marr, better than RBs/WRs available at this pick.
Tyler Warren is the last quality starting TE on the board and fills your only open slot — clear positional value over WR4/RB6 depth.
Ravens' clear WR1 and a top-15 consensus WR sliding to Rd 8 — value that rounds out our RB-heavy build. Zay Flowers is the pick.
Every-down rookie RB1 in Cleveland's backfield — starter value falling to my bench. Elite depth and trade insurance.
Talented WR at a discount post-move to Denver — best value left for bench depth.
Garrett Wilson - elite Jets WR1 talent with high ceiling for bench depth. Great value at ADP 38 vs. mid-tier RBs.
DeVonta Smith at ADP 33 is elite talent slipping late—WR1 upside for bench depth. Can't pass on this value.
McConkey is a clear ADP value here, locking in a high-target-share WR upside slot as bench depth.
Best value on the board at pick 50 — Davante Adams (ADP 46) is a proven WR1 target monster, elite bench/flex insurance.
Reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year and Carolina's clear WR1 falling well past ADP. Elite bench upside with pure WR value on an RB-heavy roster.
Egbuka is a locked-in WR2 in Tampa's high-volume passing game — best pure talent left on the board at ADP 38.
Zero backup RBs is a critical roster gap at pick 53. Swift offers immediate depth with a clear role in Chicago's offense and PPR-friendly receiving volume.
Rhamondre Stevenson offers RB depth at exact ADP with upside if NE's backfield opportunities expand. Solid bench contributor without red flags.
McLaurin at ADP 55 for pick 59 is solid value on a WR1 in Washington's offense. Best available bench upside beats reaching on RB/TE scraps.
DJ Moore falls to us 10 picks past ADP — now Josh Allen's clear WR1 in Buffalo. Elite bench WR upside with zero downside.
Best player available slides to us: Jameson Williams is a big-play WR1 threat in Detroit's high-octane offense. Pure value at pick 61.
LaPorta at ADP 57 is the best value left, a true TE1 upside stash behind Warren. Safer floor than reaching on backup RBs/WRs this deep.
Mike Evans at ADP 60 — proven downfield threat providing WR depth. Takes advantage of best available value before reaching for K/DEF.
Chuba Hubbard (ADP 66) offers RB depth with lead-back upside in PPR. Strong handcuff value and flexes well as you've maxed WR depth.
Dowdle is Pittsburgh's clear early-down back and pass-catching value; sturdy RB depth in the FLEX mix for your loaded roster.
MHJ is a former WR1 pick sliding to round 14 — league-winning bench upside at zero cost to my stacked starters.
Best leg in football on a high-scoring Cowboys offense. When a K1 falls to round 15, you take him.
Dicker's the best kicker available (top ADP, high-powered LAC offense) — last pick, take the safest leg in the league.
Jason Myers - earliest ADP available, consistent leg for Seattle. Kicker variance is noise; take the consensus pick and move on.
Strongest defense on the board. Baltimore's elite pass rush and secondary deliver consistent league-wide scoring leaders.
Steelers D at ADP — elite pass rush, takeaway upside, easy top-of-list value to close the draft.
Last pick, best D on the board — Seattle's front seven closes the draft with a sack. Legion of Boom, budget edition.

grades.summary: Elite roster construction anchored by an RB1 (Bijan), a top-tier WR (JSN), and the positional edge of Trey McBride at TE, with strong ADP value on Burrow (QB at ADP 16) and a deep, injury-clean WR corps (Collins, Flowers, Adams, McMillan, Moore). The only nitpick is late K/DEF and slightly WR-heavy depth, but the top-end talent plus zero flagged players makes this the best draft in the league.

Loaded a dominant RB room (Gibbs, Hampton, Barkley, Jacobs) plus a true WR1 in Jefferson, giving huge weekly upside, and grabbed value at TE with the Warren/LaPorta duo. Slightly redundant RB investment in early rounds (four RBs by R5) left WR depth thinner than ideal and forced later WR reaches, but it's a clean, well-balanced, injury-aware build.

Started strong with Chase, CMC, and Henry for a high-ceiling core and stayed injury-aware, but leaned on aging/declining assets (Henry, Mike Evans) and a shakier RB depth chart (Swift, Stevenson, Hubbard). Good positional balance and solid value overall, though the top-end is a notch below Opus and Sonnet and the roster carries more age risk.

Decent ADP value early (Nacua, St. Brown, Achane) but zero injury awareness sank the draft: spent premium picks on Brock Bowers (Out, meniscus surgery) and TreVeyon Henderson (Out, ankle), plus questionable tags on Nabers and Odunze. Doubling up at QB (Allen, Daniels) wasted a roster spot, and the injury exposure guts the effective depth.

An RB-heavy build with reasonable ADP value (Taylor, Cook, Lamb) is undermined by taking A.J. Brown (IR) in R5 and Jordyn Tyson (IR) in R14 with no injury awareness. Two wasted QB picks (Maye and Caleb Williams) plus the dead IR spots leave the roster thin and poorly constructed relative to the field.

lineup_log.why: Started confirmed-healthy studs (Bijan, Breece, Collins, Burrow, McBride) and used FLEX on Flowers (WR15) and back-from-injury Judkins over high-variance WRs and a questionable McMillan.

Started the highest season_avg players at each mandatory slot, then filled FLEX with the next-best RB/WR (Hampton, Jacobs) over lower WRs/TE2; confirmed via web search that Rice avoids suspension and Warren is healthy for Week 1, while Dowdle drops to a committee role behind Warren in PIT so he stays benched.
Prioritize elite talent (Chase, Jackson, Henry, Higgins) with healthy status confirmed. Fill remaining spots with highest-upside players (Smith, Wilson, Loveland) in favorable Week 1 matchups.
Start Jalen Hurts over a Questionable Joe Burrow; sit Doubtful Zay Flowers and Out Nico Collins for healthy McMillan/Judkins.
Start newly-added David Montgomery at RB2 over Barkley/Hampton; bench Questionable Ladd McConkey for Emeka Egbuka in FLEX.
Start Mike Evans and Garrett Wilson at WR over the underperforming Chase/Pickens; roll with elite RB depth in both FLEX spots.
Nico Collins sits due to Questionable status; Josh Jacobs (newly added) starts in FLEX as the clear RB1 in Green Bay's backfield.
Started the top healthy scorers by season average across the roster.
Started top season-average performers; Colston Loveland (newly added) is the only rostered TE, so starts by necessity as well as merit.

transactions.why: Jalen Hurts is a clear top-5 QB upgrade over a Questionable Joe Burrow; worth a strong bid, dropping the lowest-upside WR (Davante Adams, 4.1 avg).
Josh Jacobs is inactive (NA, 0.0 avg) and a dead roster spot; David Montgomery is the top-ADP available RB and a clear bench upgrade.
Upgrade from non-producing rookie Loveland (0.0 avg) to proven TE talent Kyle Pitts; conservative bid given an already-strong roster.
Kyle Pitts at 1.0 is essentially non-functional; Colston Loveland is a clear TE upgrade at a critical weak position.
Josh Jacobs is a healthy RB who handles most of the work in Green Bay's backfield, so he gives much more depth than Marvin Harrison's 1.9 average from an overloaded WR room.

Jaylen Warren gives clear starting-caliber RB touches in Pittsburgh's backfield, upgrading thin RB depth beyond Gibbs/Montgomery. Rico Dowdle is Questionable with a similar low average, making him the easiest drop.
